note: Reset in Phase 7. The original justification written here was wrong and has been corrected: a ~5x latency drop from the Phase 5 baseline (p95_latency_ms=5282.0) looked plausibly explained by q1's seed population growing from 25 to 99 patients (data/seed/ci_graph_seed.cypher corrected, mirroring Block 5's phase-12-fix-q1-seed), but a controlled A/B check (identical fresh-container methodology, old 25-patient seed vs. new 99-patient seed, same run sequence as the original Phase 5 baseline) found population size is NOT the explanation: the 25-patient seed measured p95=1390ms and the 99-patient seed measured p95=1219ms - essentially the same, consistent with Neo4j's index-free adjacency relationship traversal making 25 vs. 99 matching rows negligible either way. The real explanation is that Phase 5's original 5282ms was very likely a one-off cold-start outlier for that specific run (first Neo4j JVM queries after container start, general system load at the time) rather than a stable, reproducible number - repeated fresh-container runs since then (old seed, new seed, and this one) all land in the 1000-1400ms p95 range regardless of q1's population. Reset to this run's real, freshly-measured number as a fresh baseline because the old single-sample baseline was never reliable, not because the workload genuinely changed latency.
